sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive posture solidifies as Energy and Healthcare lead sustained multi-timeframe strength, while cyclical sectors suffer sharp relative rank drops.

Market breadth remains narrow with only 3 of 11 sectors posting all-green profiles across weekly through YTD timeframes. Leadership is heavily concentrated at the top, driven by Energy (momentum 0.883, YTD rank 1) and Healthcare (momentum 0.867, YTD rank 3), both showing sustained strength across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons. Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.733, YTD rank 4) is reinforcing this tilt toward safety.

Meanwhile, cyclical groups are rapidly fading. Basic Materials and Industrials both slipped 2 spots over the last 5 sessions, dropping to ranks 5 and 6 respectively. Along with deeply lagging areas like Utilities (momentum 0.183, YTD rank 10) and Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.350, YTD rank 11), capital is continuing to rotate out of economically sensitive sectors into established high-momentum leaders.

## Strength
- Energy anchors the market with top-tier leadership, holding an all-green profile, sustained top-3 multi-month rank, and the highest momentum score at 0.883.
- Healthcare joins Energy as a sustained leader, posting an all-green record across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD frames with 0.867 momentum.
- Consumer Defensive rounds out the 3 all-green groups with a momentum score of 0.733 and a YTD rank of 4.

## Movers & Momentum
- Healthcare posted the biggest short-term surge, climbing +3 spots over 5 sessions to reach rank 3.
- Basic Materials (-2 spots to rank 5, momentum 0.383) and Industrials (-2 spots to rank 6, momentum 0.283) experienced the sharpest weekly rank deterioration.
- Consumer Defensive rose +1 spot to rank 4, while Real Estate gained +1 spot to reach rank 8 despite weak 0.267 momentum.
- Momentum leaders are topped by Energy (0.883), Healthcare (0.867), Consumer Defensive (0.733), and Technology (0.717, rank 2).

## Divergences
- Utilities represents the steepest underperformance divergence, lagging the entire market with a momentum score of 0.183 at YTD rank 10.
- Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom (rank 11) with a weak 0.350 momentum score, failing to close the gap on upper-tier leadership.
- Basic Materials holds a mid-tier YTD rank of 5 but displays deteriorating momentum at 0.383 alongside its recent 2-spot rank drop.

rotation_phase.label: Defensive
rotation_phase.reasoning: Leadership is dominated by Healthcare and Consumer Defensive alongside Energy, while cyclicals like Financials lag, matching the defensive rotation profile.

- Consumer Cyclical and Consumer Defensive show weak broad-frame leadership despite recent RS crosses and 20-session RS new highs, both registering an rs_score of 0.33, an rs_confirmed of 0.11, and beating SPY on only 3/7 timeframes.
- Basic Materials reflects fragile outperformance, matching an rs_score of 0.33 and an rs_confirmed of 0.11 while beating SPY on only 3/7 timeframes without recording any positive RS crosses or new highs.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and Healthcare dominate sustained leadership, while Materials and Industrials suffer sharp near-term rank drops and Tech shows early signs of fading.

Energy and Healthcare continue to control the top of the board, underpinned by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.911 momentum, rank 1 YTD) and Diagnostics & Research (0.896 momentum). Defensive and consumer pockets are seeing rapid 5-day inflows, evidenced by sharp rank improvements in Business Equipment & Supplies (+19 spots) and Healthcare Plans (+13 spots to rank 23).

Conversely, cyclical and resource-heavy groups are retreating quickly, led lower by Engineering & Construction (-25 spots to rank 49) and Silver (-21 spots to rank 51). Simultaneously, key tech areas like Software - Infrastructure and Semiconductors are displaying negative divergence as their short-term ranks begin to slip despite elevated momentum profiles.

## Strength
- **Resilient breadth:** 28 of 144 groups maintain an all-green profile across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD frames.
- **Top-tier momentum:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.911), Diagnostics & Research (0.896), and Oil & Gas Integrated (0.875) represent the market's strongest momentum anchors.
- **Healthcare consistency:** Medical Distribution (0.872 momentum) and Health Information Services (0.869 momentum) confirm persistent strength across healthcare sub-sectors, both remaining sustained leaders across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Top 5-day rank gainers:** Business Equipment & Supplies surged +19 spots (rank 40, 0.75 momentum), Shell Companies gained +17 spots (rank 28, 0.76 momentum), and Medical Distribution advanced +15 spots (rank 40, 0.87 momentum).
- **Steepest rank drops:** Engineering & Construction fell -25 spots (rank 49, 0.32 momentum), Silver plunged -21 spots (rank 51, 0.47 momentum), and Agricultural Inputs declined -17 spots (rank 52, 0.38 momentum).
- **Deepest laggards:** Mortgage Finance (0.017 momentum, rank 142 YTD), Gambling (0.038 momentum, rank 143 YTD), and Advertising Agencies (0.094 momentum, rank 144 YTD) remain anchored at the bottom of relative performance.

## Divergences
- **Fading tech and growth:** Tech momentum leaders are slipping over the last 5 sessions, led by Software - Infrastructure (0.73 momentum, rank -5), Semiconductors (0.65 momentum, rank -6), and Internet Content & Information (0.65 momentum, rank -5).
- **Emerging early turnarounds:** Rank is accelerating ahead of low underlying momentum in Insurance Brokers (+11 spots, 0.48 momentum), Leisure (+10 spots, 0.50 momentum), and Travel Services (+6 spots, 0.48 momentum).
